item.title: 'Cut-to-fuse' strategy: A new route for molecular skeletal editing
item.description: **Problem.** Ester bonds resist selective cleavage under mild conditions, limiting how freely chemists can edit a molecule's core skeleton. **Approach.** Researchers treat hydroxycoumarins with a chlorinating agent (NCS), which "cuts" a bond via halogenation, generating an intermediate that "fuses" into a new ring — at room temperature, no metal catalyst. **Result.** Over 99% yield, tolerating a wide range of substituents. **Why it matters.** Catalyst-free, room-temperature editing is what medicinal chemists want for diverse drug-candidate structures. **Jargon:** *Ester* — bond linking a carbon chain to an oxygen-carbon group. *Halogenation* — adding a halogen atom to a molecule. *Skeletal editing* — reworking a molecule's core structure. *Catalyst* — an additive that speeds a reaction, avoided here.

item.title: New method tests magnet-powered braking for safer, more reusable spacecraft reentry
item.description: **Problem.** Reusable spacecraft need reentry heat protection, but current tiles and ablative materials are heavy and costly. **Approach.** Researchers tested MHD aerobraking: a magnetic field applied to reentry's ionized plasma, pushing the shock layer off the hull. A model was fired through a hypersonic tube at 7+ km/s with a 1.58-tesla electromagnet. **Result.** With the field on, the heated layer's thickness — a proxy for heat pushed off the hull — grew 15%+. **Why it matters.** An early proof-of-concept for magnetic, not physical, reentry shielding — less weight, less maintenance. **Jargon:** *MHD* — magnetic fields interacting with conductive fluids. *Plasma* — superheated ionized gas. *Shock layer* — compressed air ahead of a fast object. *Tesla* — unit of field strength.
